items.english: Outside the door, darkened before they knew it, there was the sound of hard wind and rain. A storm.

The parent and child had gathered at the table under the dim electric light hanging close to the wall of the narrow room, about to take their supper. The father and the mother were both still truly young. And the child was a plump little girl, just able to stand by holding to the table.
notes: くりくりと肥ってる: kuri-kuri suggests roundness and plumpness rather than curly hair; rendered as plump to keep the bodily comedy plain.

items.english: Neither the man nor the woman had yet a single wrinkle in the face. But in the man's hollowed, kindly eyes in the shadow of his thick eyebrows there was to be seen a weary colour of tiredness. And in the colour of the woman's dark hair and about her slender shoulders there was to be seen a still deeper, sunken tiredness, and a drowsy peace.
The day had ended. The sorrow and the suffering of that day were about to flow into the peace of the night. And they smiled in silence and fixed their eyes on all of the child.
notes: その子供のすべてに瞳を注いだ kept as all of the child to preserve the subete repetition rather than smoothing to everything about her.

items.english: Standing unsteadily, the child was trying with fat, round, ball-short hands to stir everything on the table, leaving not a moment's gap, and far too fast. So, smiling, they put everything, the tea-bowls and the earthen teapot and the aluminium pot, under the table. On the table there remained only the small spoon the child held and a single small plate.
notes: Tableware kept plain as poverty-modernity detail without gloss; smiling repeats the hohoemi chain.

items.english: But the child gave a noisy cry full of small joy and banged the spoon and the plate down upon the table.

data.say: Drafted the storm frame and crowded supper through the spoon-banging.
